question: A 9-year-old boy presents with abdominal pain that started nearly 6 hours ago. The pain is located in the periumbilical area and radiates to the right lower quadrant. There was no vomiting or passage of stool since the onset of pain. The patient reports that he passed stools with blood several times during the past month. The vital signs include: blood pressure 110/70 mm Hg, heart rate 81/min, respiratory rate 16/min, and temperature 37.5℃ (99.5℉). The physical examination reveals abdominal tenderness and guarding in the periumbilical area. An abdominal ultrasound does not reveal an appendiceal abnormality. The patient underwent an exploratory laparoscopy. At the time of laparoscopy, a 2-cm wide inflamed diverticulum is found 40 cm proximal to the ileocecal valve. The diverticulum is resected and sent for histologic evaluation. The result is shown in the exhibit. Which of the following statements is true?

options.opa: It resulted from traction by embryonic peritoneal adhesions.
options.opb: The most probable cause of this diverticulum is increased intraluminal pressure.
options.opc: It is an unobliterated embryonic bile duct.
options.opd: It is a remnant of the embryonic omphalomesenteric duct.

paths: (Ileocecal Valve)-PART_OF->(Entire nerve)-PART_OF->(Structure of parenchyma of lung)-LOCATION_OF->(removal technique)
(Ileocecal Valve)-PART_OF->(lymph nodes)-PART_OF->(Structure of parenchyma of lung)-LOCATION_OF->(removal technique)

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Abdominal pain in periumbilical area radiating to right lower quadrant -> No vomiting or passage of stool -> Blood in stools past month -> Vital signs stable -> Abdominal tenderness and guarding in periumbilical area -> Abdominal ultrasound normal -> Exploratory laparoscopy -> Inflamed diverticulum found 40 cm proximal to ileocecal valve -> Diverticulum resected -> Histologic evaluation performed -> Result shown in exhibit -> 95%
enhanced_information: The inflamed diverticulum found during laparoscopy is most likely due to increased intraluminal pressure rather than other causes such as embryonic peritoneal adhesions, an unobliterated embryonic bile duct, or a remnant of the embryonic omphalomesenteric duct. The diverticulum is not a false diverticulum. The histologic evaluation result supports the probable cause being increased intraluminal pressure.
analysis: The core medical principle here is to consider the most likely cause of the inflamed diverticulum based on the enhanced information provided. The exhibit and the enhanced information strongly suggest that the diverticulum is due to increased intraluminal pressure rather than other causes like embryonic peritoneal adhesions, an unobliterated embryonic bile duct, or a remnant of the embryonic omphalomesenteric duct. The histologic evaluation result further supports this conclusion.
